“Commission”), 18 C.F.R. § 35.13 (2026), Ohio Valley Electric Corporation (“OVEC”),
an Ohio corporation submits for filing the following:1

      x   Engineering and Design Agreement between OVEC and East Kentucky Power
          Cooperative, Inc. (“EKPC”) (under PJM Service Agreement No. 8085) associated
          with OVEC’s performance of an engineering and design study related to a new
          interconnection point between OVEC and EKPC (“Carroll County Engineering and
          Design Agreement”).

and design study, at EKPC’s expense,2 with respect to a potential project in which an
EKPC 345 kV transmission line would interconnect at a new OVEC 345 kV station located

                        ENGINEERING AND DESIGN AGREEMENT

               FOR THE CARROLL COUNTY DATA CENTER PROJECT

        This Engineering and Design Agreement for the Carroll County Data Center Project
(the “Agreement”) is entered into as of September 23, 2026 (the “Execution Date”) by and between
Ohio Valley Electric Corporation, an Ohio corporation (“OVEC”), and East Kentucky Power
Cooperative, Inc., a Kentucky corporation (“EKPC”). OVEC and EKPC are each individually
referred to as a “Party” and collectively referred to as the “Parties.”


                                           RECITALS

       A.       EKPC desires that OVEC perform an engineering and design study with respect to
a potential project in which an EKPC 345 kV transmission line would interconnect at a new OVEC
345 kV station located in Carroll County, Kentucky (the “Project”) to be constructed and owned
by OVEC or one of its Affiliates. The purpose of the Project is to facilitate EKPC serving a 720
MW load for one of its retail customers.

        B.      OVEC is willing to perform the engineering and design study for the Project as set
forth in this Agreement.

                                        AGREEMENTS

NOW, THEREFORE, the Parties hereby agree as follows:

1.     DEFINITIONS; RULES OF CONSTRUCTION

      1.1.    Definitions. As used in this Agreement, terms defined in Exhibit A have the
meanings set forth therein.

        1.2.    Rules of Construction. Unless the context of this Agreement requires otherwise,
the plural includes the singular, and the singular includes the plural. The words “include,”
“includes,” and “including” are not limiting and have the inclusive meaning of “including without
limitation.” The words “hereof,” “herein,” “hereby,” “hereunder,” and other similar terms of this
Agreement refer to this Agreement as a whole and not exclusively to any particular provision of
this Agreement. All pronouns and any variations thereof will be deemed to refer to masculine,
feminine, neuter, singular, or plural, as the identity of the Person or Persons may require. Unless
otherwise expressly provided, any agreement, instrument, or Applicable Law defined or referred
to herein means such agreement, instrument or Applicable Law as from time to time amended,
modified, or supplemented, including (in the case of agreements or instruments) by waiver or
consent and (in the case of Applicable Law) by succession of comparable successor law and
includes (in the case of agreements or instruments) references to all attachments thereto and
instruments incorporated therein. A reference to a Party includes its successors and permitted
assigns. The headings contained in this Agreement are solely for the convenience of the Parties
and shall not be used or relied upon in any manner in the construction or interpretation of this
Agreement. Unless otherwise specified, references in this Agreement to numbered sections,
articles, and exhibits shall be to sections, articles and exhibits of this Agreement. This Agreement

                                                                                              Page 1
 is the result of negotiations between, and has been reviewed by, the Parties, and their respective
counsel have had the opportunity to review this Agreement. Accordingly, this Agreement shall be
deemed to be the product of all Parties hereto, and no ambiguity shall be construed in favor of or
against any Party.

2.     EFFECTIVE DATE; TERM; TERMINATION

        2.1.     Effective Date. OVEC shall file this Agreement with FERC and EKPC agrees to
cooperate with OVEC and provide reasonable assistance to OVEC in such filing and proceedings
related thereto. This Agreement shall become effective on the date deemed effective by FERC
(“Effective Date”). In connection with such filing, if FERC imposes any conditions, limitations
or qualifications which individually or in the aggregate are determined by OVEC or EKPC to be
adverse to it, then either Party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice to the other Party.

        2.2.   Term. The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and
unless earlier terminated pursuant to Section 2.3, shall terminate sixty (60) Calendar Days
following the completion of all work and other activities as provided for hereunder and satisfaction
of all payment obligations of the Parties hereunder, if any.

       2.3.    Events of Termination. This Agreement may be terminated by the Parties as
follows:

               2.3.1.   This Agreement may be terminated by mutual written agreement of the
                        Parties.

               2.3.2.   Either EKPC or OVEC may terminate this Agreement as provided in
                        Section 2.1.

               2.3.3.   Either EKPC or OVEC may terminate this Agreement if: (a) any
                        Governmental Authority denies approval of any necessary or appropriate
                        approvals for any of the work under this Agreement; (b) a Party ceases to
                        maintain any Governmental Approval necessary for such Party’s
                        performance of this Agreement or the contemplated ownership or
                        operation of the Project facilities; or (c) any Governmental Authority shall
                        have issued an order, decree, ruling, or other action restraining, enjoining,
                        or otherwise prohibiting a Party’s performance of this Agreement or its
                        contemplated ownership or operation of the Project facilities.

               2.3.4.   Either Party may terminate this Agreement for continued Force Majeure
                        as provided in Section 6.1.

               2.3.5.   Either Party may terminate this Agreement for default as provided in
                        Section 7.2.

        2.4.    Regulatory Approval of Termination. No termination hereunder shall become
effective until the terminating Party (or the Parties jointly) tenders to FERC any required
notification of termination of this Agreement and obtains acceptance thereof by FERC as may be
required.


                                                                                               Page 2
         2.5.    Survival of Rights. Termination of this Agreement shall not relieve the Parties of
obligations under this Agreement that by their nature should survive such termination (including,
without limitation, cost responsibility, payment obligations, remedies, indemnification
obligations, limitations of liability, and confidentiality), and each Party may take whatever judicial
or administrative actions as necessary or desirable to enforce its rights hereunder, subject to the
governing law provisions hereof.

3.     ENGINEERING & DESIGN

       3.1. Engineering & Design. Upon receipt of the Initial Payment referenced in Section
4.2.1, OVEC shall commence an engineering and design study for the Project (“Engineering
Work”). OVEC shall prepare a report (the “Engineering Report”) which shall include:

               3.1.1.   The OVEC facilities to be constructed;

               3.1.2.   A proposed single-line diagram of the OVEC facilities including the
                        interconnection point with the EKPC facilities;

               3.1.3.   The EKPC facilities necessary for interconnection with the OVEC
                        facilities;

               3.1.4.   OVEC’s estimated costs to construct its facilities for the Project;

               3.1.5.   An estimate of the amount of time needed to complete the construction
                        after EKPC submits an Election to Proceed with Project; and

               3.1.6.   Sag Study results.

      3.2.   Schedule. OVEC shall exercise commercially reasonable efforts to deliver the
Engineering Report within one hundred twenty (120) Calendar Days after receipt of the Initial
Payment and completion of the PJM Attachment M-3 process as set forth in Section 3.4 below.

       3.3.  Standards. OVEC will perform the Engineering Work in accordance with
Applicable Law and Good Utility Practice.

       3.4.    PJM Review. EKPC acknowledges and agrees that this Agreement includes OVEC
submitting to PJM the Engineering Report, so that such plans can be reviewed by PJM in their
Attachment M-3 process or other applicable process(es). As a part of the Attachment M-3 process,
PJM will perform a Do No Harm analysis. If PJM’s Do No Harm analysis concludes that the
OVEC facilities for the Project would cause additional reliability violations to those listed in a
previous load study, OVEC may either modify the design of the facilities for the Project and/or
modify the construction schedule for the facilities for the Project to be constructed and resubmit
such modified plans to PJM for review. EKPC agrees that any potential costs of such
modifications shall be included as part of the cost of OVEC’s Engineering Report.

       3.5.    Election to Proceed with Project. Within sixty (60) Calendar Days after receipt of
the Engineering Report, EKPC must provide a written notice to OVEC that EKPC is either (a)
requesting OVEC to enter into a construction agreement to undertake construction activities for
the Project (“Election to Proceed with Project”) or (b) notifying OVEC that it does not wish to
proceed with construction of the Project. OVEC’s obligation to undertake any construction
                                                                                                Page 3
 activities is subject to execution of a construction agreement and receipt of any necessary
Governmental Approvals for such construction agreement. If EKPC does not provide an Election
to Proceed with Project within the sixty (60) Calendar Day period, then EKPC shall be deemed to
have elected to not move forward with construction activities.

4.     COSTS

       4.1.   OVEC Costs.

              4.1.1.   EKPC shall be responsible for paying all of OVEC’s actual costs with
                       respect to the Engineering Work described in Article 3 (such costs the
                       “Study Costs”).

              4.1.2.   The Study Costs will include all reasonable costs, charges, and expenses
                       incurred by OVEC in connection with the Engineering Work, including
                       overhead and other internal costs or charges and third party expenses.

       4.2.   Invoicing and Payment

              4.2.1.   Within fifteen (15) Calendar Days after the Effective Date, EKPC shall
                       make an initial payment to OVEC in the amount of $175,000 (the “Initial
                       Payment”) to be applied to the Study Costs as defined in Section 4.1.

              4.2.2.   Within sixty (60) days after completion of the Engineering Work, OVEC
                       shall provide to EKPC a statement of its final actual costs for the
                       Engineering Work. If the statement of final actual costs identifies that the
                       actual costs exceeded OVEC’s cost estimate, EKPC shall pay the
                       difference between the actual cost and cost estimate within thirty (30) days
                       after OVEC sends the final invoice to EKPC. If OVEC’s actual costs for
                       the Engineering Work are less than the amount of OVEC’s cost estimate,
                       the unused portion of any advance payment shall be returned to EKPC
                       within thirty (30) days after issuance of the statement of the final actual
                       cost. If EKPC in good faith disputes any portion of the statement, EKPC
                       will pay the undisputed amount of the statement when due, and EKPC will
                       provide a written explanation for disputing part of the statement no later
                       than the date that payment is due. Representatives of the Parties shall meet
                       as expeditiously as possible to resolve the dispute. Once the dispute is
                       resolved and if it has been determined that a Party owes payment, such
                       Party will pay all amounts determined to be due within fifteen (15)
                       Calendar Days following resolution of the dispute.

              4.2.3.   Payment shall be made by electronic transfer or such other means as the
                       Parties may mutually agree upon. From and after the due date, unpaid
                       amounts will accrue interest daily at the then-current Prime Rate plus two
                       percent (2%) per annum, but will in no event exceed the maximum interest
                       rate allowed pursuant to Applicable Law.




                                                                                             Page 4
 5.      DISCLAIMER OF WARRANTY; LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

      5.1. DISCLAIMER OF WARRANTY. EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN SECTION 3.3,
OVEC DOES NOT MAKE AND EXPRESSLY DISCLAIMS ANY EXPRESS OR IMPLIED
WARRANTIES, INCLUDING WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, NON-
INFRINGEMENT OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE OR ANY WARRANTY
THAT ITS WORK WILL BE ERROR FREE OR UNINTERRUPTED.

      5.2.  LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. NOTWITHSTANDING ANYTHING IN THIS
AGREEMENT TO THE CONTRARY, NO PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE UNDER ANY
PROVISION OF, OR BASED ON, THIS AGREEMENT FOR ANY SPECIAL, INDIRECT,
INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, PUNITIVE, OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES
(INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, LOSS OF PROFIT OR REVENUE, LOSS OF
BUSINESS, LOSS OF USE OF EQUIPMENT, COST OF CAPITAL, OR DAMAGE TO
REPUTATION OR RELATIONS) WHETHER BASED IN CONTRACT, TORT, STRICT
LIABILITY, STATUTORY LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER THEORY OF LIABILITY EVEN
IF APPRISED OF THE LIKELIHOOD OF SUCH DAMAGES OCCURRING.

6.      FORCE MAJEURE

        6.1. Effect of Force Majeure. In the event that any Party is rendered unable by reason
of an event of Force Majeure to perform, wholly or in part, any obligation or commitment set forth
in this Agreement, then the obligations of such Party (except for the obligation to pay sums of
money owing hereunder for periods prior to the event of Force Majeure) shall be suspended to the
extent of such Force Majeure condition, and such Party shall not be deemed to be in breach of this
Agreement, for the period of such Force Majeure condition. The affected Party shall exercise
commercially reasonable efforts to rectify the conditions brought about by the Force Majeure and
to avoid or minimize delay. Either Party may terminate this Agreement if the Force Majeure
extends for more than one (1) year.

        6.2.   Notification. In the event of the occurrence of an event of Force Majeure which
prevents a Party from performing its obligations hereunder, the affected Party shall promptly notify
the other Party of such Force Majeure after the determination that an event of Force Majeure has
occurred.

        6.3.    Labor Disputes. Neither Party will be required by this Agreement to settle any
strike, walkout, lockout, or other labor dispute on terms which, in the sole judgment of the Party
involved in the dispute, are contrary to its interest, it being understood that the settlement of strikes,
walkouts, lockouts, or other labor disputes will be at the sole discretion of the Party having the
difficulty.

7.      DEFAULT AND REMEDIES

        7.1.    Events of Default. An “Event of Default” will exist:

                7.1.1.   As to EKPC, upon EKPC’s failure to pay any undisputed amount due
                         under this Agreement on or before the payment date therefor, which failure
                         is not cured within ten (10) Calendar Days following written notice by
                         OVEC of such failure;

                                                                                                    Page 5
                7.1.2.   As to a Party, if such Party fails to fully cure its breach of any other
                        obligation under this Agreement within twenty (20) Calendar Days
                        following written notification of such breach or such longer period, not to
                        exceed a total cure period of one hundred eighty (180) Calendar Days, as
                        may be reasonably necessary to cure such breach, provided that such Party
                        has commenced and is diligently pursuing such cure;

               7.1.3.   As to a Party, if such Party assigns this Agreement in a manner inconsistent
                        with the terms of this Agreement; or

               7.1.4.   As to a Party if it becomes Insolvent.

        7.2.    Termination. If an Event of Default in any material respect occurs as to a Party,
the other Party will have the right to terminate this Agreement upon written notice to the defaulting
Party.

       7.3.    Other Remedies.

               7.3.1.   If an Event of Default in any material respect occurs and while it persists
                        with respect to a Party, the other Party may suspend performance of its
                        obligations under this Agreement (other than its obligations to pay money)
                        without prejudice to any other remedy that it may have under this
                        Agreement or Applicable Law.

               7.3.2.   Whether or not a Party suspends performance of its obligations under, or
                        terminates, this Agreement as a result of an Event of Default, such Party
                        will have the right to recover from the defaulting Party all amounts due
                        hereunder, plus all other damages and remedies to which it is entitled at
                        law or in equity due to such Event of Default, subject to the limitations of
                        Article 5.

8.     CONFIDENTIALITY

        8.1.    Confidential Information. For purposes of this Agreement, a Party’s “Confidential
Information” consists of information related to the Project possessed by that Party which is
confidential and commercially valuable and which is disclosed by such Party on or after the
Execution Date of this Agreement in connection with the Engineering Work. For purposes of this
Agreement, the Party providing Confidential Information is the “Disclosing Party,” and the Party
receiving Confidential Information is the “Receiving Party.” Confidential Information will not
include any information which the Receiving Party can demonstrate (a) has become available to
the public through no breach of this Agreement; (b) was previously known by the Receiving Party
without any obligation to hold it in confidence; (c) was received on a non-confidential basis from
a third party free to disclose such information without restriction; or (d) was independently
developed by the Receiving Party without the use of Confidential Information of the Disclosing
Party. For purposes of this Agreement, a Party will be deemed to have received Confidential
Information of the other Party if such Confidential Information is by any means disclosed or
delivered to the Receiving Party or any of its or its Affiliates’ equity owners, directors, managers,
officers, employees, advisors, attorneys, contractors, consultants, or agents (its “Representatives”).


                                                                                                Page 6
         8.2.    Non-Disclosure. Except as provided in this Section 8.2 and in Section 8.3, each
Party hereto agrees that it shall hold in strict confidence and shall not disclose or use any
Confidential Information belonging to a Disclosing Party for the period ending eighteen (18)
months after the expiration of the Term or earlier termination of this Agreement. Notwithstanding
the foregoing, a Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to its Representatives for
purposes of meeting its obligations and exercising its rights hereunder, provided that the
Representatives shall be informed of the confidentiality obligations provided herein. Each Party
agrees to be responsible for any breach of the confidentiality obligations under this Agreement by
its Representatives.

         8.3.    Required Disclosures. If a Receiving Party is required pursuant to Applicable Law
or otherwise becomes legally compelled to disclose any of the Confidential Information or the fact
that the Confidential Information has been made available to it, such Receiving Party shall (unless
prohibited by Applicable Law from doing so) promptly notify the Disclosing Party prior to such
disclosure in order that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or such other remedy as
the Disclosing Party may consider appropriate in the circumstances. In any event, the Receiving
Party may disclose only that portion of the Confidential Information which such Receiving Party
is legally required to disclose in the judgment of the Receiving Party’s legal counsel without any
liability to the Disclosing Party hereunder and such disclosure shall not be a breach of this Article
8.

       8.4.    Return or Destruction. The Receiving Party, upon written request from the
Disclosing Party, shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information in its possession
and the Receiving Party shall destroy its Evaluation Materials. If requested by the Disclosing
Party, the Receiving Party shall provide the Disclosing Party with a certification that all
Confidential Information and Evaluation Materials have either been returned or destroyed, as
applicable. The return or destruction of the Confidential Information shall not extinguish any
rights or obligations under this Agreement with respect to the Confidential Information.
Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Receiving Party shall not be required to purge any historical
backup media and may retain one or more copies of the Confidential Information solely for
archival purposes and as required by Applicable Law.

9.     GENERAL

       9.1.    Scope of Agreement. This Agreement provides for OVEC to perform certain
engineering work with respect to the Project. This Agreement does not provide for any other
services and neither OVEC nor EKPC agrees hereunder to provide any other services.

        9.2.    Regulatory Authorities. This Agreement is made subject to the jurisdiction of any
Governmental Authority having jurisdiction in the premises. Except for each Party’s termination
rights, which are governed by Section 2.3 of this Agreement, nothing contained in this Agreement
shall be construed as affecting in any way the right of a Party, as the case may be, to unilaterally
file with FERC an application for a change in rates, charges, classification, or service, or of any
rule, regulation, or contract relating thereto pursuant to Section 205 or 206 of the Federal Power
Act and FERC’s rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.

       9.3.    Notices.


                                                                                               Page 7
                9.3.1.   Administrative Notices. Any notice that is required or permitted under this
                        Agreement may be given by personal delivery to the Party entitled thereto,
                        by e-mail (with confirmation of receipt), by any courier service which
                        guarantees overnight, receipted delivery, or by U.S. certified or registered
                        mail, return receipt requested, addressed to the Party entitled thereto, at the
                        addresses set forth in Exhibit B. Either Party may change its address for
                        notice by written notice to the other Party in accordance with this Section.
                        Such change will not necessitate a filing under Section 205 of the Federal
                        Power Act.

               9.3.2.   Invoices and Payments. Invoices and payments shall be sent to the
                        addresses for invoices and payments set out in Exhibit B. EKPC may
                        change its address for invoices by giving thirty (30) Calendar Days written
                        notice prior to the effective date of the change. Such change will not
                        necessitate a filing under Section 205 of the Federal Power Act.

       9.4.    Assignment. This Agreement shall inure to the benefit of and be binding upon the
successors and assigns of the Parties. This Agreement shall not be assigned by any Party without
the written consent of the other Party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld,
conditioned, or delayed.

        9.5.   Merger and Integration; Binding on Successors; No Third Party Beneficiaries. This
Agreement sets out the entire understanding of the Parties with respect to the matters it purports
to cover and supersedes all prior communications, agreements, and understandings, whether
written or oral, concerning such matters. No Party will be liable or bound to any Party in any
manner by any warranties, representations, or covenants other than those set forth in or
incorporated into this Agreement. The terms and conditions of this Agreement will inure to the
benefit of and be binding upon the respective successors and permitted assigns of the Parties.
Nothing in this Agreement, express or implied, is intended to confer upon any third party any
rights, remedies, obligations, or liabilities under or by reason of this Agreement, except as
expressly provided in this Agreement.

        9.6. Amendment. Except for a Party’s right to request that FERC unilaterally amend
the Agreement pursuant to Section 205 or Section 206 of the Federal Power Act or FERC’s
authority to amend the Agreement under Section 206 of the Federal Power Act, this Agreement
may not be amended except by a written instrument executed by the Parties hereto.

       9.7.   Forbearance and Waiver. Except where a specific time period is provided
hereunder for the exercise of a right or remedy, any Party’s forbearance in the exercise or
enforcement of any right or remedy under this Agreement will not constitute a waiver thereof, and
a waiver under one circumstance will not constitute a waiver under any other circumstance.

       9.8.   Partial Invalidity. Any invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability of any provision of
this Agreement in any jurisdiction will not invalidate or render illegal or unenforceable the
remaining provisions hereof in such jurisdiction and will not invalidate or render illegal or
unenforceable such provision in any other jurisdiction.

      9.9. Governing Law. The interpretation, enforcement, and performance of this
Agreement shall be governed by federal law where applicable, and when not in conflict with or
                                                                                                 Page 8
 preempted by federal law, the laws of the State of Kentucky, without regard to the laws of such
jurisdiction applicable to conflict of laws.

        9.10. Multiple Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed by the Parties in multiple
original counterparts, and each such counterpart will constitute an original hereof, but all of which
together will constitute one instrument. An executed copy of this Agreement, and any amendments
hereto, to the extent signed and delivered by means of an attachment to an electronic mail message
in “pdf” or similar format, shall be treated in all manner and respects as an original agreement and
shall be considered to have the same binding legal effect as if it were the original signed version
thereof.

        9.11. No Partnership. Nothing contained herein shall be deemed to create an association,
joint venture, partnership, or principal/agent relationship between the Parties hereto or impose any
partnership obligation or liability on either Party. No Party shall have any right, power, or
authority to enter into any agreement or commitment, act on behalf of, or otherwise bind the other
Party in any way.

                        ENGINEERING AND DESIGN AGREEMENT

               FOR THE CARROLL COUNTY DATA CENTER PROJECT

        This Engineering and Design Agreement for the Carroll County Data Center Project
(the “Agreement”) is entered into as of September 23, 2026 (the “Execution Date”) by and between
Ohio Valley Electric Corporation, an Ohio corporation (“OVEC”), and East Kentucky Power
Cooperative, Inc., a Kentucky corporation (“EKPC”). OVEC and EKPC are each individually
referred to as a “Party” and collectively referred to as the “Parties.”


                                           RECITALS

        A.     EKPC desires that OVEC perform an engineering and design study with respect to a
potential project in which an EKPC 345 kV transmission line would interconnect at a new OVEC
345 kV station located in Carroll County, Kentucky (the “Project”) to be constructed and owned by
OVEC or one of its Affiliates. The purpose of the Project is to facilitate EKPC serving a 720 MW
load for one of its retail customers.

        B.      OVEC is willing to perform the engineering and design study for the Project as set
forth in this Agreement.

                                        AGREEMENTS

NOW, THEREFORE, the Parties hereby agree as follows:

1.     DEFINITIONS; RULES OF CONSTRUCTION

     1.1.   Definitions.  As used in this Agreement, terms defined in Exhibit
AExh1point1Exh1point1Exh1point1 have the meanings set forth therein.

        1.2.   Rules of Construction. Unless the context of this Agreement requires otherwise, the
plural includes the singular, and the singular includes the plural. The words “include,” “includes,”
and “including” are not limiting and have the inclusive meaning of “including without limitation.”
The words “hereof,” “herein,” “hereby,” “hereunder,” and other similar terms of this Agreement
refer to this Agreement as a whole and not exclusively to any particular provision of this
Agreement. All pronouns and any variations thereof will be deemed to refer to masculine,
feminine, neuter, singular, or plural, as the identity of the Person or Persons may require. Unless
otherwise expressly provided, any agreement, instrument, or Applicable Law defined or referred to
herein means such agreement, instrument or Applicable Law as from time to time amended,
modified, or supplemented, including (in the case of agreements or instruments) by waiver or
consent and (in the case of Applicable Law) by succession of comparable successor law and
includes (in the case of agreements or instruments) references to all attachments thereto and
instruments incorporated therein. A reference to a Party includes its successors and permitted
assigns. The headings contained in this Agreement are solely for the convenience of the Parties
and shall not be used or relied upon in any manner in the construction or interpretation of this
 Agreement. Unless otherwise specified, references in this Agreement to numbered sections,
articles, and exhibits shall be to sections, articles and exhibits of this Agreement. This Agreement
is the result of negotiations between, and has been reviewed by, the Parties, and their respective
counsel have had the opportunity to review this Agreement. Accordingly, this Agreement shall be
deemed to be the product of all Parties hereto, and no ambiguity shall be construed in favor of or
against any Party.

2.     EFFECTIVE DATE; TERM; TERMINATION

        2.1.     Effective Date. OVEC shall file this Agreement with FERC and EKPC agrees to
cooperate with OVEC and provide reasonable assistance to OVEC in such filing and proceedings
related thereto. This Agreement shall become effective on the date deemed effective by FERC
(“Effective Date”). In connection with such filing, if FERC imposes any conditions, limitations or
qualifications which individually or in the aggregate are determined by OVEC or EKPC to be
adverse to it, then either Party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice to the other Party.

        2.2.   Term. The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and
unless earlier terminated pursuant to Section 2.3, shall terminate sixty (60) Calendar Days
following the completion of all work and other activities as provided for hereunder and satisfaction
of all payment obligations of the Parties hereunder, if any.

       2.3.    Events of Termination. This Agreement may be terminated by the Parties as
follows:

               2.3.1.   This Agreement may be terminated by mutual written agreement of the
                        Parties.

               2.3.2.   Either EKPC or OVEC may terminate this Agreement as provided in
                        Section 2.1.

               2.3.3.   Either EKPC or OVEC may terminate this Agreement if: (a) any
                        Governmental Authority denies approval of any necessary or appropriate
                        approvals for any of the work under this Agreement; (b) a Party ceases to
                        maintain any Governmental Approval necessary for such Party’s
                        performance of this Agreement or the contemplated ownership or
                        operation of the Project facilities; or (c) any Governmental Authority shall
                        have issued an order, decree, ruling, or other action restraining, enjoining,
                        or otherwise prohibiting a Party’s performance of this Agreement or its
                        contemplated ownership or operation of the Project facilities.

               2.3.4.   Either Party may terminate this Agreement for continued Force Majeure as
                        provided in Section 6.1.

               2.3.5.   Either Party may terminate this Agreement for default as provided in
                        Section 7.2.




                                                 2
         2.4.    Regulatory Approval of Termination. No termination hereunder shall become
effective until the terminating Party (or the Parties jointly) tenders to FERC any required
notification of termination of this Agreement and obtains acceptance thereof by FERC as may be
required.

        2.5.    Survival of Rights. Termination of this Agreement shall not relieve the Parties of
obligations under this Agreement that by their nature should survive such termination (including,
without limitation, cost responsibility, payment obligations, remedies, indemnification
obligations, limitations of liability, and confidentiality), and each Party may take whatever judicial
or administrative actions as necessary or desirable to enforce its rights hereunder, subject to the
governing law provisions hereof.

3.     ENGINEERING & DESIGN

       3.1.  Engineering & Design. Upon receipt of the Initial Payment referenced in Section
4.2.1, OVEC shall commence an engineering and design study for the Project (“Engineering
Work”). OVEC shall prepare a report (the “Engineering Report”) which shall include:

               3.1.1.   The OVEC facilities to be constructed;

               3.1.2.   A proposed single-line diagram of the OVEC facilities including the
                        interconnection point with the EKPC facilities;

               3.1.3.   The EKPC facilities necessary for interconnection with the OVEC
                        facilities;

               3.1.4.   OVEC’s estimated costs to construct its facilities for the Project;

               3.1.5.   An estimate of the amount of time needed to complete the construction
                        after EKPC submits an Election to Proceed with Project; and

               3.1.6.   Sag Study results.

      3.2.   Schedule. OVEC shall exercise commercially reasonable efforts to deliver the
Engineering Report within one hundred twenty (120) Calendar Days after receipt of the Initial
Payment and completion of the PJM Attachment M-3 process as set forth in Section 3.4 below.

       3.3.  Standards. OVEC will perform the Engineering Work in accordance with
Applicable Law and Good Utility Practice.

       3.4.    PJM Review. EKPC acknowledges and agrees that this Agreement includes OVEC
submitting to PJM the Engineering Report, so that such plans can be reviewed by PJM in their
Attachment M-3 process or other applicable process(es). As a part of the Attachment M-3 process,
PJM will perform a Do No Harm analysis. If PJM’s Do No Harm analysis concludes that the
OVEC facilities for the Project would cause additional reliability violations to those listed in a
previous load study, OVEC may either modify the design of the facilities for the Project and/or
modify the construction schedule for the facilities for the Project to be constructed and resubmit


                                                  3
 such modified plans to PJM for review. EKPC agrees that any potential costs of such modifications
shall be included as part of the cost of OVEC’s Engineering Report.

        3.5.   Election to Proceed with Project. Within sixty (60) Calendar Days after receipt of
the Engineering Report, EKPC must provide a written notice to OVEC that EKPC is either (a)
requesting OVEC to enter into a construction agreement to undertake construction activities for the
Project (“Election to Proceed with Project”) or (b) notifying OVEC that it does not wish to proceed
with construction of the Project. OVEC’s obligation to undertake any construction activities is
subject to execution of a construction agreement and receipt of any necessary Governmental
Approvals for such construction agreement. If EKPC does not provide an Election to Proceed with
Project within the sixty (60) Calendar Day period, then EKPC shall be deemed to have elected to
not move forward with construction activities.

4.     COSTS

       4.1.    OVEC Costs.

               4.1.1.   EKPC shall be responsible for paying all of OVEC’s actual costs with
                        respect to the Engineering Work described in Article 3 (such costs the
                        “Study Costs”).

               4.1.2.   The Study Costs will include all reasonable costs, charges, and expenses
                        incurred by OVEC in connection with the Engineering Work, including
                        overhead and other internal costs or charges and third party expenses.

       4.2.    Invoicing and Payment

               4.2.1.   Within fifteen (15) Calendar Days after the Effective Date, EKPC shall
                        make an initial payment to OVEC in the amount of $175,000 (the “Initial
                        Payment”) to be applied to the Study Costs as defined in Section 4.1.

               4.2.2.   Within sixty (60) days after completion of the Engineering Work, OVEC
                        shall provide to EKPC a statement of its final actual costs for the
                        Engineering Work. If the statement of final actual costs identifies that the
                        actual costs exceeded OVEC’s cost estimate, EKPC shall pay the
                        difference between the actual cost and cost estimate within thirty (30) days
                        after OVEC sends the final invoice to EKPC. If OVEC’s actual costs for
                        the Engineering Work are less than the amount of OVEC’s cost estimate,
                        the unused portion of any advance payment shall be returned to EKPC
                        within thirty (30) days after issuance of the statement of the final actual
                        cost. If EKPC in good faith disputes any portion of the statement, EKPC
                        will pay the undisputed amount of the statement when due, and EKPC will
                        provide a written explanation for disputing part of the statement no later
                        than the date that payment is due. Representatives of the Parties shall meet
                        as expeditiously as possible to resolve the dispute. Once the dispute is
                        resolved and if it has been determined that a Party owes payment, such



                                                 4
                          Party will pay all amounts determined to be due within fifteen (15)
                         Calendar Days following resolution of the dispute.

                4.2.3.   Payment shall be made by electronic transfer or such other means as the
                         Parties may mutually agree upon. From and after the due date, unpaid
                         amounts will accrue interest daily at the then-current Prime Rate plus two
                         percent (2%) per annum, but will in no event exceed the maximum interest
                         rate allowed pursuant to Applicable Law.

5.      DISCLAIMER OF WARRANTY; LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

      5.1. DISCLAIMER OF WARRANTY. EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN SECTION 3.3,
OVEC DOES NOT MAKE AND EXPRESSLY DISCLAIMS ANY EXPRESS OR IMPLIED
WARRANTIES, INCLUDING WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, NON-
INFRINGEMENT OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE OR ANY WARRANTY
THAT ITS WORK WILL BE ERROR FREE OR UNINTERRUPTED.

      5.2.  LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. NOTWITHSTANDING ANYTHING IN THIS
AGREEMENT TO THE CONTRARY, NO PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE UNDER ANY
PROVISION OF, OR BASED ON, THIS AGREEMENT FOR ANY SPECIAL, INDIRECT,
INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, PUNITIVE, OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES
(INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, LOSS OF PROFIT OR REVENUE, LOSS OF
BUSINESS, LOSS OF USE OF EQUIPMENT, COST OF CAPITAL, OR DAMAGE TO
REPUTATION OR RELATIONS) WHETHER BASED IN CONTRACT, TORT, STRICT
LIABILITY, STATUTORY LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER THEORY OF LIABILITY EVEN IF
APPRISED OF THE LIKELIHOOD OF SUCH DAMAGES OCCURRING.

6.      FORCE MAJEURE

       6.1.    Effect of Force Majeure. In the event that any Party is rendered unable by reason of
an event of Force Majeure to perform, wholly or in part, any obligation or commitment set forth in
this Agreement, then the obligations of such Party (except for the obligation to pay sums of money
owing hereunder for periods prior to the event of Force Majeure) shall be suspended to the extent
of such Force Majeure condition, and such Party shall not be deemed to be in breach of this
Agreement, for the period of such Force Majeure condition. The affected Party shall exercise
commercially reasonable efforts to rectify the conditions brought about by the Force Majeure and
to avoid or minimize delay. Either Party may terminate this Agreement if the Force Majeure
extends for more than one (1) year.

        6.2.   Notification. In the event of the occurrence of an event of Force Majeure which
prevents a Party from performing its obligations hereunder, the affected Party shall promptly notify
the other Party of such Force Majeure after the determination that an event of Force Majeure has
occurred.

        6.3.    Labor Disputes. Neither Party will be required by this Agreement to settle any
strike, walkout, lockout, or other labor dispute on terms which, in the sole judgment of the Party
involved in the dispute, are contrary to its interest, it being understood that the settlement of strikes,


                                                    5
 walkouts, lockouts, or other labor disputes will be at the sole discretion of the Party having the
difficulty.

7.     DEFAULT AND REMEDIES

       7.1.    Events of Default. An “Event of Default” will exist:

               7.1.1.   As to EKPC, upon EKPC’s failure to pay any undisputed amount due
                        under this Agreement on or before the payment date therefor, which failure
                        is not cured within ten (10) Calendar Days following written notice by
                        OVEC of such failure;

               7.1.2.   As to a Party, if such Party fails to fully cure its breach of any other
                        obligation under this Agreement within twenty (20) Calendar Days
                        following written notification of such breach or such longer period, not to
                        exceed a total cure period of one hundred eighty (180) Calendar Days, as
                        may be reasonably necessary to cure such breach, provided that such Party
                        has commenced and is diligently pursuing such cure;

               7.1.3.   As to a Party, if such Party assigns this Agreement in a manner inconsistent
                        with the terms of this Agreement; or

               7.1.4.   As to a Party if it becomes Insolvent.

       7.2.    Termination. If an Event of Default in any material respect occurs as to a Party, the
other Party will have the right to terminate this Agreement upon written notice to the defaulting
Party.

       7.3.    Other Remedies.

               7.3.1.   If an Event of Default in any material respect occurs and while it persists
                        with respect to a Party, the other Party may suspend performance of its
                        obligations under this Agreement (other than its obligations to pay money)
                        without prejudice to any other remedy that it may have under this
                        Agreement or Applicable Law.

               7.3.2.   Whether or not a Party suspends performance of its obligations under, or
                        terminates, this Agreement as a result of an Event of Default, such Party
                        will have the right to recover from the defaulting Party all amounts due
                        hereunder, plus all other damages and remedies to which it is entitled at
                        law or in equity due to such Event of Default, subject to the limitations of
                        Article 5.

8.     CONFIDENTIALITY

       8.1.    Confidential Information. For purposes of this Agreement, a Party’s “Confidential
Information” consists of information related to the Project possessed by that Party which is
confidential and commercially valuable and which is disclosed by such Party on or after the

                                                 6
 Execution Date of this Agreement in connection with the Engineering Work. For purposes of this
Agreement, the Party providing Confidential Information is the “Disclosing Party,” and the Party
receiving Confidential Information is the “Receiving Party.” Confidential Information will not
include any information which the Receiving Party can demonstrate (a) has become available to
the public through no breach of this Agreement; (b) was previously known by the Receiving Party
without any obligation to hold it in confidence; (c) was received on a non-confidential basis from a
third party free to disclose such information without restriction; or (d) was independently
developed by the Receiving Party without the use of Confidential Information of the Disclosing
Party. For purposes of this Agreement, a Party will be deemed to have received Confidential
Information of the other Party if such Confidential Information is by any means disclosed or
delivered to the Receiving Party or any of its or its Affiliates’ equity owners, directors, managers,
officers, employees, advisors, attorneys, contractors, consultants, or agents (its “Representatives”).

        8.2.    Non-Disclosure. Except as provided in this Section 8.2 and in Section 8.3, each
Party hereto agrees that it shall hold in strict confidence and shall not disclose or use any
Confidential Information belonging to a Disclosing Party for the period ending eighteen (18)
months after the expiration of the Term or earlier termination of this Agreement. Notwithstanding
the foregoing, a Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to its Representatives for
purposes of meeting its obligations and exercising its rights hereunder, provided that the
Representatives shall be informed of the confidentiality obligations provided herein. Each Party
agrees to be responsible for any breach of the confidentiality obligations under this Agreement by
its Representatives.

         8.3.    Required Disclosures. If a Receiving Party is required pursuant to Applicable Law
or otherwise becomes legally compelled to disclose any of the Confidential Information or the fact
that the Confidential Information has been made available to it, such Receiving Party shall (unless
prohibited by Applicable Law from doing so) promptly notify the Disclosing Party prior to such
disclosure in order that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or such other remedy as
the Disclosing Party may consider appropriate in the circumstances. In any event, the Receiving
Party may disclose only that portion of the Confidential Information which such Receiving Party is
legally required to disclose in the judgment of the Receiving Party’s legal counsel without any
liability to the Disclosing Party hereunder and such disclosure shall not be a breach of this Article
8.

        8.4.    Return or Destruction. The Receiving Party, upon written request from the
Disclosing Party, shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information in its possession and
the Receiving Party shall destroy its Evaluation Materials. If requested by the Disclosing Party, the
Receiving Party shall provide the Disclosing Party with a certification that all Confidential
Information and Evaluation Materials have either been returned or destroyed, as applicable. The
return or destruction of the Confidential Information shall not extinguish any rights or obligations
under this Agreement with respect to the Confidential Information. Notwithstanding the foregoing,
the Receiving Party shall not be required to purge any historical backup media and may retain one
or more copies of the Confidential Information solely for archival purposes and as required by
Applicable Law.




                                                  7
 9.      GENERAL

       9.1.    Scope of Agreement. This Agreement provides for OVEC to perform certain
engineering work with respect to the Project. This Agreement does not provide for any other
services and neither OVEC nor EKPC agrees hereunder to provide any other services.

        9.2.    Regulatory Authorities. This Agreement is made subject to the jurisdiction of any
Governmental Authority having jurisdiction in the premises. Except for each Party’s termination
rights, which are governed by Section 2.3 of this Agreement, nothing contained in this Agreement
shall be construed as affecting in any way the right of a Party, as the case may be, to unilaterally file
with FERC an application for a change in rates, charges, classification, or service, or of any rule,
regulation, or contract relating thereto pursuant to Section 205 or 206 of the Federal Power Act and
FERC’s rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.

        9.3.    Notices.

                9.3.1.     Administrative Notices. Any notice that is required or permitted under this
                           Agreement may be given by personal delivery to the Party entitled thereto,
                           by e-mail (with confirmation of receipt), by any courier service which
                           guarantees overnight, receipted delivery, or by U.S. certified or registered
                           mail, return receipt requested, addressed to the Party entitled thereto, at the
                           addresses set forth in Exhibit B. Either Party may change its address for
                           notice by written notice to the other Party in accordance with this Section.
                           Such change will not necessitate a filing under Section 205 of the Federal
                           Power Act.

                9.3.2.     Invoices and Payments. Invoices and payments shall be sent to the
                           addresses for invoices and payments set out in Exhibit B. EKPC may
                           change its address for invoices by giving thirty (30) Calendar Days written
                           notice prior to the effective date of the change. Such change will not
                           necessitate a filing under Section 205 of the Federal Power Act.

       9.4.    Assignment. This Agreement shall inure to the benefit of and be binding upon the
successors and assigns of the Parties. This Agreement shall not be assigned by any Party without
the written consent of the other Party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld,
conditioned, or delayed.

         9.5.   Merger and Integration; Binding on Successors; No Third Party Beneficiaries. This
Agreement sets out the entire understanding of the Parties with respect to the matters it purports to
cover and supersedes all prior communications, agreements, and understandings, whether written
or oral, concerning such matters. No Party will be liable or bound to any Party in any manner by
any warranties, representations, or covenants other than those set forth in or incorporated into this
Agreement. The terms and conditions of this Agreement will inure to the benefit of and be binding
upon the respective successors and permitted assigns of the Parties. Nothing in this Agreement,
express or implied, is intended to confer upon any third party any rights, remedies, obligations, or
